intent: I'm done replacing headphones every two years. Headbands crack, earpads flake, batteries give up. This time I want one pair of over-ears I can still be wearing in 2036, even if that means paying more up front or going wired. What actually kills headphones over the years, and does going wireless doom me from the start because of the battery? Do replaceable pads and cables genuinely matter or is that a spec-sheet gimmick? I want to hear what long-term owners say survived a decade of daily use, and then the one pair you'd bet on.

intent_v1_legacy: Our new puppy has turned me into an anxious mess of conflicting advice. The pet store insists grain-free food is healthier, my sister swears raw feeding cured her dog's allergies, the bowls brag about being BPA-free, and there are calming chews with L-theanine and dental chews that supposedly replace brushing. My vet was vague and I honestly can't tell what's proven versus pet-industry marketing. Can you dig into whether each of those claims actually holds up, why companies get away with saying this stuff, and what I should actually buy for him based on what's genuinely supported?
